body:
I don't know, it feels a bit bloaty IMHO. I think the proposal might need a bit more backing before we implement this.

Also, I am not sure the implementation is enough. IIRC, you cannot set on a TileSet a polygon that has less than 3 points, as it would be not valid. That probably means the default editor won't work on an empty polygon. This will need to fixed before being merged.

I had not considered how it would behave if the polygon had less than 3 points. I agree that needs to be investigated, to ensure that at least it doesn't cause a crash or anything like that.

Regarding the general idea of including a way to manually set vertex coordinates, I feel it is essential for good UX and workflow support. The proposal and subsequent PR was inspired by me using some unusual collision shapes (i.e., not just filling the tile) and needing the shapes to line up perfectly across different tiles. While I could get an okayish approximation by dragging the vertices, the numbers were still off; ultimately, I opened the .tres file for the TileSet in my IDE and changed the numbers there. This worked, but was awful UX.

I'm not aware of anywhere else in the Godot editor (or any professional software at all, really) where a visual drag-and-drop editor is provided, but there is no way to manually set numbers/coordinates as well. I will elaborate more in the proposal thread later today it would fit better there, to keep this PR thread dedicated to the specific implementation itself.

As for "bloat", keep in mind that the array is collapsed by default and can be collapsed at any time, making it just a single line in the inspector when collapsed. Users can expand it to modify the vertex positions as necessary, then collapse it once they're done. It will have a minimal impact on the length of the property list when collapsed, but will massively improve the usability of the editor for professional, thorough workflows.

When the user tries to delete a vertex from a polygon with only 3 vertices, the array is unmodified and an error toast message appears telling them that a polygon needs at least 3 vertices. 

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57381c6c-e9ce-4cba-9f61-c6fc3439c1e0

I don't recall seeing editor functionality for disabling the delete buttons in an array, and IMO other than the message calling the error "internal", I think this would be a fine way to handle it.

> When the user tries to delete a vertex from a polygon with only 3 vertices, the array is unmodified and an error toast message appears telling them that a polygon needs at least 3 vertices.

Well, yeah, but the "Add element" button won't work either if the polygon is empty. The error message is fine but the problem is that you cannot create a polygon out of nothing with this editor, which makes the UX a bit bad.

A solution would be to allow polygons of size 1 et 2, and edit TileMapLayer and its editor so they are ignored. I think it would be acceptable even if it means spreading checks everywhere.

The PR now no longer throws errors when a polygon with 1 or 2 points is created; it treats it the same as a polygon with 0 points, telling the physics engine that there is no polygon at all (to my understanding). 

This seems to work well overall; the caveat is that, at the moment, the editor GUI doesn't display the polygon points if there are only one or two of them, instead making it look like there is no polygon. The property inspector doesn't have any major indication of an issue with the property value (i.e., displaying a warning message that the current polygon points are invalid). As such, I could potentially see people not realizing they have a polygon with 1 or 2 points, and being confused as to why their polygon isn't showing up.
(Collision)Polygon2D already behave the same way, so it's fine.

I've made some updates to the PR:

- The condition checks for displaying the property in the inspector are removed, so it'll show the property as part of the default behavior.
- I found a couple of spots where we were checking for the emptiness of the polygon point count, and replaced them with `< 3` checks. 
- Now, if there are less than 3 points in the polygon, a ConvexPolygonShape2D is still created for it with those points and pushed to the shape array. I thought this would be good to keep the counts for shape and polygon data in sync for consistency's sake, but I'm not entirely sure it's necessary. Let me know if it doesn't make sense to do this, and I can certainly remove it.

As per your statement about the getter and setter APIs, it might be wise for me to set up a little test that sets then gets polygons that are both valid and invalid, and confirms that the data is 1:1.

In my testing, there are two user experience issues I've noticed that I want to tackle eventually:
- The visual editor doesn't show anything for polygons with < 3 points. I think it would be preferable to draw *something* at the existing vertices. Can't remember how to achieve it at the moment, but I recall there being a condition where red Xs were drawn at the vertices instead of the white diamonds, to indicate they were invalid - we could do something like that here.
- Polygons with < 3 points don't seem to be saved. If I create a polygon in the editor and make it have 2 points, then save, close, and reopen the editor, the polygon is entirely gone and I have to recreate it from scratch. It's not the *worst* thing, since people shouldn't be caring about invalid polygons or wanting to save them anyways, but having data just disappear is also not great 😅
